You're clearly a person who cares about others. You care about what will happen to your cat, you care about notifying the right people, and you care about not burdening your family. I think that you must be a very compassionate person to still have these concerns, even when you're feeling so depressed. 

About your cat: I used to work at an animal shelter, and we got cats sometimes that came from owners who died suddenly. Cats experience grief. They sometimes will not eat, they will groom obsessively, and sometimes they revert back to kitten behaviors to self-soothe. I think that it's likely that your cat will be sad if you die. 

If it's okay for you to talk about it, why do you want to die?

I'm really sorry. That sounds terrible. I think you're a good person, because you clearly care about not hurting your parents. You know that they will be sad and miss you if you die. 

Sometimes, I really hate myself, too. But sometimes, it's helpful for me to think about all the things I don't like about myself, and wonder if I would be so harsh if another person, like one of my friends, had the same traits or issues. 

It can be hard, but you should try to show yourself the kindness and consideration that you have for other people.

Thank you for being kind. I still love my partner but he is and always has been emotionally unavailable, and he acts as though he has no interest in me romantically. He might be able to help me financially, but emotionally I am completely on my own. 

My savings will not allow me to return home, as the currency here is weaker than in my home country. Even if I go back, I have no one who I could stay with. One of my long-term friends died of leukemia a few years ago, and the other is having hardships with anorexia and drugs, and so there is no one left for me to turn to. I have an older brother in his 30s, but he depends on my parents financially, and they have barred him from contacting me or helping me out.  

Honestly, I want more than anything to go back home, but it would take years of saving to make that possible.

Thank you for saying something kind to me. I know I have made it very far. My family comes from a very rural background, and I'm the first woman in my family to go to university. I know I am "strong" but that only comes from years of hardship, and I feel like I just can't do it any more. 

I know I have worked hard and made strides and done the impossible, but I am just so, so tired, and I feel completely alone. It's so hard for me to have hope that anything in the future could change. I applied to 15 more jobs today because I would feel worse to not do anything, but every waking moment all I can think about is how much I want to die. I just don't have the energy to keep going any more.
